```{r}
  Pct_Missing = round(sapply(SIMOA_analysis, function(x) 100 * mean(is.na(x))), 1),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

var_inventory$Domain <- dplyr::case_when(
  var_inventory$Variable == "scrn_stopped_bzra"                        ~ "OUTCOME",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% core_demographics                        ~ "Demographics",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% health_vars                              ~ "Clinical: Health",
  var_inventory$Variable == "c_lengthofuse"                            ~ "Clinical: Length of Use",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% med_burden_vars                          ~ "Clinical: Medication Burden",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% condition_counts                         ~ "Clinical: Condition Counts",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% bzra_dose_vars                           ~ "Clinical: BZRA Dose",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% sleep_aids                               ~ "Behavioural: Sleep Aids",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% c(side_effects_items, safety_items,
                                 adl_items, dependence_items)          ~ "Clinical: Adverse Effects",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% c(withdrawal_combined, withdrawal_count) ~ "Clinical: Withdrawal",
  var_inventory$Variable == stop_rate_var                              ~ "Clinical: Stop Rate",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% comb_vars                               ~ "Behavioural: COM-B",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% bmq_items                               ~ "Clinical: BMQ Necessity (raw items)",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% reasons_vars                            ~ "Behavioural: Reasons",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% dbas_items                              ~ "Personality: DBAS",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% bfi_items_scored                        ~ "Personality: BFI",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% surps_items_scored                      ~ "Personality: SURPS",
  var_inventory$Variable %in% ciss_items                              ~ "Personality: CISS",
  TRUE                                                                 ~ "Other"
)

for(dom in sort(unique(var_inventory$Domain))) {
  sub_df <- var_inventory[var_inventory$Domain == dom, ]
  cat(sprintf("── %s (%d variable%s) ──\n",
              dom, nrow(sub_df), ifelse(nrow(sub_df) == 1, "", "s")))
  print(sub_df[, c("Variable", "Class", "N_Complete", "N_Missing", "Pct_Missing")],
        row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\n")
}

write.csv(var_inventory, "variable_inventory.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("✓ Saved: variable_inventory.csv\n\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART I: COLUMN NAME PRINTOUT FOR IMPUTATION VERIFICATION

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART I: COLUMN NAMES FOR IMPUTATION VERIFICATION\n")

cat(sprintf("SIMOA_analysis contains %d variables across %d observations.\n\n",
            ncol(SIMOA_analysis), nrow(SIMOA_analysis)))

col_df <- data.frame(

cat("ALL VARIABLES TO BE IMPUTED:\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

saveRDS(SIMOA_analysis, "SIMOA_analysis.rds")

analysis_variables <- list(
```

## Diagnostics - MI
```{r}
#==============================================================================
# CHUNK 7: PRE-IMPUTATION DIAGNOSTICS & OPTIMIZATION
#==============================================================================
# Purpose: Comprehensive diagnostics before multiple imputation
# Outputs: Statistically-derived m and maxit, optimized imputation parameters
#
# KEY METHODS:
#   m     → Von Hippel (2020) two-stage FMI-based quadratic rule
#             DOI: 10.1177/0049124117747303
#             Package: howManyImputations (Errickson, CRAN)
#   maxit → Empirical convergence experiment (m=5, maxit=10/20/30/40)
#             Gelman-Rubin PSRF < 1.1 criterion
#             Gelman & Rubin (1992); Brooks & Gelman (1998)
#==============================================================================

# install.packages(c("howManyImputations", "coda"))

library(mice)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(car)
library(coda)             # Gelman-Rubin PSRF via chainMean (convergence check)
library(howManyImputations)

cat("\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PRE-IMPUTATION DIAGNOSTICS & OPTIMIZATION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

# Load prepared dataset from Chunk 6
if(file.exists("SIMOA_analysis.rds")) {
  SIMOA_analysis <- readRDS("SIMOA_analysis.rds")
  analysis_vars  <- readRDS("analysis_variable_lists.rds")
  cat("✓ Loaded SIMOA_analysis.rds from Chunk 6\n")
  cat("  Dimensions:", nrow(SIMOA_analysis), "rows ×", ncol(SIMOA_analysis), "columns\n\n")
} else {
  stop("ERROR: SIMOA_analysis.rds not found. Please run Chunk 6 first.")
}

# Verify reverse coding was done
cat("VERIFICATION: Checking reverse coding from Chunk 6\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
if(!is.null(analysis_vars$bfi_reversed) && length(analysis_vars$bfi_reversed) > 0) {
  cat("✓ BFI items reversed in Chunk 6:", length(analysis_vars$bfi_reversed), "\n")
  cat("  Items:", paste(analysis_vars$bfi_reversed, collapse = ", "), "\n")
} else {
  cat("⚠️  No BFI reverse coding detected\n")
}
if(!is.null(analysis_vars$surps_reversed) && length(analysis_vars$surps_reversed) > 0) {
  cat("✓ SURPS items reversed in Chunk 6:", length(analysis_vars$surps_reversed), "\n")
  cat("  Items:", paste(analysis_vars$surps_reversed, collapse = ", "), "\n")
} else {
  cat("⚠️  No SURPS reverse coding detected\n")
}
cat("\n")

# Remove outcome from imputation dataset
outcome <- analysis_vars$outcome
if(outcome %in% names(SIMOA_analysis)) {
  df_imp <- SIMOA_analysis %>% select(-all_of(outcome))
  cat("✓ Removed outcome variable:", outcome, "\n")
  cat("  Imputation dataset:", nrow(df_imp), "rows ×", ncol(df_imp), "columns\n\n")
} else {
  df_imp <- SIMOA_analysis
  cat("⚠️  Outcome variable not found in dataset\n\n")
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART A: COMPREHENSIVE MISSINGNESS DIAGNOSTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART A: COMPREHENSIVE MISSINGNESS DIAGNOSTICS\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

n_total        <- nrow(df_imp)
n_vars         <- ncol(df_imp)
missing_counts <- colSums(is.na(df_imp))
missing_pct    <- 100 * missing_counts / n_total
total_cells    <- n_total * n_vars
total_missing  <- sum(missing_counts)
pct_missing_overall <- 100 * total_missing / total_cells

cat("OVERALL MISSINGNESS:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  Total observations:", n_total, "\n")
cat("  Total variables:",    n_vars,  "\n")
cat("  Total cells:",        total_cells, "\n")
cat("  Missing cells:",      total_missing, "(", round(pct_missing_overall, 2), "%)\n")
cat("  Complete cases:",     sum(complete.cases(df_imp)),
    "(", round(100 * sum(complete.cases(df_imp)) / n_total, 1), "%)\n\n")

vars_with_missing <- names(missing_counts[missing_counts > 0])
vars_complete     <- names(missing_counts[missing_counts == 0])

cat("VARIABLE-LEVEL MISSINGNESS:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  Variables with missing data:", length(vars_with_missing), "\n")
cat("  Variables complete:",          length(vars_complete),     "\n\n")

miss_cats <- cut(missing_pct,
                 breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 25, 40, 100),
                 labels = c("Minimal (<5%)", "Low (5-10%)", "Moderate (10-25%)",
                            "High (25-40%)", "Very High (>40%)"),
                 include.lowest = TRUE)

cat("MISSINGNESS SEVERITY:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat(sprintf("  Minimal (<5%%):      %3d variables\n", sum(miss_cats == "Minimal (<5%)",     na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("  Low (5-10%%):        %3d variables\n", sum(miss_cats == "Low (5-10%)",       na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("  Moderate (10-25%%):  %3d variables\n", sum(miss_cats == "Moderate (10-25%)", na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("  High (25-40%%):      %3d variables\n", sum(miss_cats == "High (25-40%)",     na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("  Very High (>40%%):   %3d variables\n\n", sum(miss_cats == "Very High (>40%)", na.rm = TRUE)))

cat("TOP 20 VARIABLES BY MISSINGNESS:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
top_missing <- head(sort(missing_pct[missing_pct > 0], decreasing = TRUE), 20)
for(i in seq_along(top_missing)) {
  cat(sprintf("  %2d. %-30s: %5.1f%% (%4d obs)\n",
              i, names(top_missing)[i], top_missing[i],
              round(top_missing[i] * n_total / 100)))
}
cat("\n")

miss_summary <- data.frame(
  variable    = names(missing_pct),
  n_missing   = missing_counts,
  pct_missing = missing_pct,
  category    = miss_cats
) %>% arrange(desc(pct_missing))

write.csv(miss_summary, "pre_imputation_missingness_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("✓ Saved: pre_imputation_missingness_summary.csv\n\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART B: VARIABLE VALIDATION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART B: VARIABLE VALIDATION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

# B1. Constant and near-zero variance
cat("B1. Checking for constant/near-zero variance variables\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")

constant_vars <- character()
nzv_vars      <- character()

for(var in names(df_imp)) {
  if(is.numeric(df_imp[[var]])) {
    non_na   <- na.omit(df_imp[[var]])
    n_unique <- length(unique(non_na))
    if(n_unique <= 1) {
      constant_vars <- c(constant_vars, var)
      cat("  ⚠️  Constant:", var, "(", n_unique, "unique value)\n")
    } else if(length(non_na) > 0) {
      var_val <- var(non_na)
      if(var_val < 1e-10) {
        nzv_vars <- c(nzv_vars, var)
        cat("  ⚠️  Near-zero variance:", var, "(SD =", round(sqrt(var_val), 6), ")\n")
      }
    }
  } else if(is.factor(df_imp[[var]])) {
    non_na   <- na.omit(df_imp[[var]])
    n_unique <- length(unique(non_na))
    if(n_unique <= 1) {
      constant_vars <- c(constant_vars, var)
      cat("  ⚠️  Single-level factor:", var, "\n")
    }
  }
}
if(length(constant_vars) == 0 && length(nzv_vars) == 0)
  cat("  ✓ No constant or near-zero variance variables detected\n")
cat("\n")

# B2. Minimum sample size
cat("B2. Checking minimum sample size (non-missing observations)\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")

low_n_vars <- character()
for(var in names(df_imp)) {
  n_obs <- sum(!is.na(df_imp[[var]]))
  if(n_obs < 10 && n_obs < n_total) {
    low_n_vars <- c(low_n_vars, var)
    cat("  ⚠️  Low sample size:", var, "(n =", n_obs, ")\n")
  }
}
if(length(low_n_vars) == 0)
  cat("  ✓ All variables have adequate sample size (n ≥ 10)\n")
cat("\n")

# B3. Separation check — factors only
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# IMPORTANT: This check is restricted to factor variables only.
# Numeric Likert-scale items (SURPS, CISS, BFI, DBAS, side-effect ratings,
# safety ratings, benefit ratings) must NOT be flagged here, even if they
# have sparse response categories. Separation is only a problem for variables
# modelled with logreg/polr/polyreg. PMM handles sparse numeric values
# without any convergence risk, so including them here would incorrectly
# remove them from the predictor matrix and reduce imputation quality.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("B3. Checking for separation in binary/categorical variables\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  Note: Check restricted to factor variables (logreg/polr/polyreg targets).\n")
cat("  Numeric Likert items are excluded — sparse counts are not a\n")
cat("  separation risk for PMM and should remain in the predictor matrix.\n\n")

separation_vars <- character()
for(var in names(df_imp)) {
  # FIX: only check true factor variables, not numeric Likert items
  if(is.factor(df_imp[[var]])) {
    non_na <- na.omit(df_imp[[var]])
    if(length(non_na) > 0) {
      freq_table <- table(non_na)
      if(any(freq_table < 5)) {
        separation_vars <- c(separation_vars, var)
        cat("  ⚠️  Sparse levels:", var, "(min count =", min(freq_table), ")\n")
      }
    }
  }
}
if(length(separation_vars) == 0)
  cat("  ✓ No separation issues detected\n")
cat("\n")

# B4. Derived variables
cat("B4. Handling derived/composite variables\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")

derived_vars <- c("n_health_conditions")
if(any(derived_vars %in% names(df_imp))) {
  cat("  ISSUE: n_health_conditions is derived (sum of component counts)\n")
  cat("         Removing to prevent perfect collinearity in imputation\n\n")
  for(var in derived_vars) {
    if(var %in% names(df_imp)) {
      df_imp <- df_imp %>% select(-all_of(var))
      cat("  ✓ Removed:", var, "(will be recalculated post-imputation)\n")
    }
  }
  cat("  Remaining variables:", ncol(df_imp), "\n\n")
  cat("  POST-IMPUTATION: n_health_conditions will be recalculated as:\n")
  cat("    n_physical_conditions + n_ment_conditions + n_sleep_conditions\n\n")
} else {
  cat("  ✓ No derived variables to remove\n\n")
}

problematic_vars <- unique(c(constant_vars, nzv_vars, low_n_vars, derived_vars))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART C: MULTICOLLINEARITY CHECK (VIF)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART C: MULTICOLLINEARITY CHECK (VIF)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

cat("PURPOSE: High multicollinearity can cause imputation instability.\n")
cat("  • VIF < 5:   Acceptable\n")
cat("  • VIF 5-10:  Moderate concern\n")
cat("  • VIF > 10:  High multicollinearity (consider removing)\n\n")

numeric_complete <- df_imp %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  select(where(~sum(is.na(.)) == 0))

cat("ELIGIBLE VARIABLES FOR VIF (complete numeric only):\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
if(ncol(numeric_complete) > 0) {
  for(i in 1:ncol(numeric_complete))
    cat(sprintf("  %2d. %s\n", i, names(numeric_complete)[i]))
  cat("\nTotal eligible:", ncol(numeric_complete), "variables\n\n")
} else {
  cat("  No complete numeric variables found\n\n")
}

# Initialise redundant_predictors so it is always defined for Part D
redundant_predictors <- character()

if(ncol(numeric_complete) >= 3) {
  vif_result <- tryCatch({
    cor_matrix    <- cor(numeric_complete, use = "complete.obs")
    upper_tri_cor <- cor_matrix[upper.tri(cor_matrix)]
    max_cor       <- max(abs(upper_tri_cor))

    if(max_cor > 0.99) {
      cat("  ⚠️  Perfect/near-perfect correlation detected (r =", round(max_cor, 3), ")\n")
      # ── Use upper.tri to find off-diagonal pairs at any correlation ≥ 0.99 ──
      # The previous condition (abs(cor) > 0.99 & abs(cor) < 1) incorrectly
      # excluded pairs with r = exactly 1.000, which is the case for
      # bzra_daily_diazepam_eq ↔ bzra_weekly_diazepam_eq (weekly = daily × 7).
      # upper.tri() selects only the upper triangle, avoiding the diagonal
      # (self-correlations of 1.0) and duplicate pairs.
      # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      perfect_pairs <- which(abs(cor_matrix) >= 0.99 & upper.tri(cor_matrix), arr.ind = TRUE)

      # ── Identify and store redundant predictors ──────────────────────────
      # For each perfectly correlated pair, the second variable (column index)
      # is flagged as redundant and will be zeroed as a predictor column below,
      # preventing chain instability. Both variables can still be imputed if
      # needed (complete variables are skipped by mice automatically).
      #
      # In this dataset the expected pair is:
      #   bzra_daily_diazepam_eq ↔ bzra_weekly_diazepam_eq
      # Weekly dose = daily dose × 7, so r = 1 by construction. Both are
      # complete (no imputation needed), so only their predictor role matters.
      # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

      if(nrow(perfect_pairs) > 0) {
        cat("     Perfectly correlated pairs:\n")
        seen_pairs <- character()
        for(i in 1:nrow(perfect_pairs)) {
          v1 <- rownames(cor_matrix)[perfect_pairs[i, 1]]
          v2 <- colnames(cor_matrix)[perfect_pairs[i, 2]]
          pair_key <- paste(sort(c(v1, v2)), collapse = "↔")
          if(!pair_key %in% seen_pairs) {
            cat("       •", v1, "↔", v2,
                sprintf("(r = %.4f — redundant as predictor: %s)\n",
                        cor_matrix[perfect_pairs[i,1], perfect_pairs[i,2]], v2))
            redundant_predictors <- c(redundant_predictors, v2)
            seen_pairs <- c(seen_pairs, pair_key)
          }
        }
      }
      cat("     Skipping VIF due to perfect multicollinearity\n\n")
      NULL

    } else {
      vif_formula <- as.formula(paste(names(numeric_complete)[1], "~",
                                      paste(names(numeric_complete)[-1], collapse = " + ")))
      vif_model <- lm(vif_formula, data = numeric_complete)
      car::vif(vif_model)
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("  ⚠️  VIF calculation failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n\n")
    NULL
  })

  if(!is.null(vif_result)) {
    vif_df <- data.frame(variable = names(vif_result), VIF = as.numeric(vif_result)) %>%
      arrange(desc(VIF))

    cat("VIF RESULTS:\n")
    cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
    for(i in 1:nrow(vif_df)) {
      status <- if(vif_df$VIF[i] < 5) "✓" else if(vif_df$VIF[i] < 10) "⚠️" else "✗"
      cat(sprintf("  %s %2d. %-30s: VIF = %6.2f\n",
                  status, i, vif_df$variable[i], vif_df$VIF[i]))
    }
    high_vif <- vif_df %>% filter(VIF > 10)
    mod_vif  <- vif_df %>% filter(VIF >= 5 & VIF <= 10)
    low_vif  <- vif_df %>% filter(VIF < 5)
    cat(sprintf("\n  ✓ Low VIF (<5):        %3d variables\n", nrow(low_vif)))
    cat(sprintf("  ⚠️ Moderate VIF (5-10): %3d variables\n", nrow(mod_vif)))
    cat(sprintf("  ✗ High VIF (>10):      %3d variables\n\n", nrow(high_vif)))
    if(nrow(high_vif) > 0) {
      cat("⚠️  VARIABLES WITH HIGH VIF — CONSIDER REMOVING:\n")
      for(i in 1:nrow(high_vif))
        cat(sprintf("  %2d. %-30s: VIF = %.2f\n", i, high_vif$variable[i], high_vif$VIF[i]))
      cat("\n")
    }
    write.csv(vif_df, "vif_analysis.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    cat("✓ Saved: vif_analysis.csv\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("ℹ️  Not enough complete numeric variables for VIF analysis\n\n")
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART D: DEFINE VARIABLE TYPES FOR IMPUTATION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART D: DEFINING VARIABLE TYPES FOR IMPUTATION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

continuous_vars <- c(
  "age",
  "med_quant", "phq2_score", "osss_3_score",
  "n_physical_conditions", "n_ment_conditions", "n_sleep_conditions",
  "wdl_symptom_count",
  "bzra_daily_diazepam_eq", "bzra_weekly_diazepam_eq",
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$dbas))  analysis_vars$dbas  else character(),
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$bfi))   analysis_vars$bfi   else character(),
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$surps)) analysis_vars$surps else character(),
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$ciss))  analysis_vars$ciss  else character()
)

binary_vars <- c("sex")

ordered_vars <- c(
  "education", "income", "employment", "driving_freq",
  "gen_health",
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$sleep_aids))      analysis_vars$sleep_aids      else character(),
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$adverse_effects)) analysis_vars$adverse_effects else character(),
  "stop_wdl_exp_combined"
)

unordered_categorical <- c(paste0("stop_wdl_exp___", 0:4))

# Filter to variables present in df_imp
continuous_vars       <- continuous_vars[continuous_vars %in% names(df_imp)]
binary_vars           <- binary_vars[binary_vars %in% names(df_imp)]
ordered_vars          <- ordered_vars[ordered_vars %in% names(df_imp)]
unordered_categorical <- unordered_categorical[unordered_categorical %in% names(df_imp)]

cat("VARIABLE TYPE ASSIGNMENT:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  Continuous (PMM):               ", length(continuous_vars), "variables\n")
cat("  Binary (logreg):                ", length(binary_vars), "variables\n")
cat("  Ordered categorical (polr):     ", length(ordered_vars), "variables\n")
cat("  Unordered categorical (polyreg):", length(unordered_categorical), "variables\n")
cat("  Total assigned:                 ",
    length(continuous_vars) + length(binary_vars) +
    length(ordered_vars) + length(unordered_categorical), "\n\n")

cat("NOTE: BZRA dose variables assigned to continuous (PMM):\n")
for(v in c("bzra_daily_diazepam_eq", "bzra_weekly_diazepam_eq")) {
  if(v %in% continuous_vars)
    cat(sprintf("  ✓ %s\n", v))
  else
    cat(sprintf("  ⚠️  %s not found in df_imp\n", v))
}
cat("\n")

# ── Force personality scale items to numeric ──────────────────────────────────
# CISS, SURPS, BFI, and DBAS items are Likert-scale integers.
# They must be numeric (not ordered factors) so mice uses PMM, not polr.
# This also prevents them appearing as sparse categorical variables, which
# causes separation warnings and chain instability.
# Note: BFI and SURPS lists from analysis_vars already contain _r names
# for reversed items — those are also forced to numeric here.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("FORCING PERSONALITY SCALE ITEMS TO NUMERIC:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  Rationale: Likert items are treated as continuous (PMM).\n")
cat("  Forcing to integer prevents accidental ordered-factor encoding\n")
cat("  which assigns polr and causes sparse-level separation warnings.\n\n")

scale_vars_all <- c(
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$dbas))  analysis_vars$dbas  else character(),
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$bfi))   analysis_vars$bfi   else character(),
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$surps)) analysis_vars$surps else character(),
  if(!is.null(analysis_vars$ciss))  analysis_vars$ciss  else character()
)
scale_vars_all <- scale_vars_all[scale_vars_all %in% names(df_imp)]

n_converted <- 0
n_already   <- 0
for(var in scale_vars_all) {
  if(!is.numeric(df_imp[[var]])) {
    df_imp[[var]] <- as.integer(df_imp[[var]])
    n_converted   <- n_converted + 1
  } else {
    n_already <- n_already + 1
  }
}

cat(sprintf("  ✓ Converted to integer: %d items\n", n_converted))
cat(sprintf("  ✓ Already numeric:      %d items\n", n_already))
cat(sprintf("  Scales covered: DBAS (%d), BFI (%d), SURPS (%d), CISS (%d)\n\n",
            sum(analysis_vars$dbas  %in% scale_vars_all),
            sum(analysis_vars$bfi   %in% scale_vars_all),
            sum(analysis_vars$surps %in% scale_vars_all),
            sum(analysis_vars$ciss  %in% scale_vars_all)))

# ── Convert remaining variables to proper types ───────────────────────────────
cat("Converting remaining variables to proper types...\n")

for(var in continuous_vars)
  if(!is.numeric(df_imp[[var]]))
    df_imp[[var]] <- as.numeric(as.character(df_imp[[var]]))
for(var in binary_vars)
  df_imp[[var]] <- as.numeric(df_imp[[var]])
for(var in ordered_vars)
  if(!is.ordered(df_imp[[var]]))
    df_imp[[var]] <- factor(df_imp[[var]], ordered = TRUE)
for(var in unordered_categorical)
  if(!is.factor(df_imp[[var]]) || is.ordered(df_imp[[var]]))
    df_imp[[var]] <- factor(df_imp[[var]], ordered = FALSE)

cat("✓ Variable type conversion complete\n\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Set up mice methods and predictor matrix
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

init   <- mice(df_imp, maxit = 0, print = FALSE)
method <- init$method

# ── quickpred(): limit predictors per imputation model ───────────────────────
# Default mice uses ALL variables as predictors for each imputed variable.
# With large questionnaire datasets this causes chain instability.
# quickpred() keeps only variables with meaningful correlation to the target.
#
# mincor = 0.10 → only predictors with |r| ≥ 0.10
#                 targets ~15–25 predictors per model (Van Buuren, 2018 §6.3)
#
# minpuc = 0.1  → exclude predictor pairs where fewer than 10% of cases
#                 have both variables observed simultaneously.
#                 This directly addresses within-scale block missingness:
#                 all 21 CISS items (or 23 SURPS, 16 DBAS) are missing
#                 together for the same respondents. Without minpuc, these
#                 items all appear as predictors for each other, creating a
#                 rank-deficient design matrix in the PMM linear model and
#                 generating "dropped predictor" logged events. minpuc = 0.1
#                 removes these low-overlap pairs from the predictor matrix
#                 before the ridge penalty is even needed.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("Building predictor matrix with quickpred()...\n")
cat("  mincor = 0.10 (minimum |r| to be included as predictor)\n")
cat("  minpuc = 0.10 (minimum proportion of usable cases — excludes\n")
cat("           block-missing within-scale pairs, Van Buuren, 2018 §6.3)\n")
cat("  Target: 15–25 predictors per model (Van Buuren, 2018 §6.3)\n\n")

pred <- quickpred(
  df_imp,
  mincor = 0.10,
  minpuc = 0.10
)

# Manually remove near-perfectly correlated predictors (|r| > 0.95)
cat("Removing near-perfectly correlated predictors (|r| > 0.95)...\n")
numeric_vars_for_cor <- names(df_imp)[sapply(df_imp, is.numeric)]
if(length(numeric_vars_for_cor) >= 2) {
  cor_matrix     <- cor(df_imp[, numeric_vars_for_cor], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  high_cor_pairs <- which(abs(cor_matrix) > 0.95 & abs(cor_matrix) < 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
  n_zeroed       <- 0
  if(nrow(high_cor_pairs) > 0) {
    for(k in 1:nrow(high_cor_pairs)) {
      row_var <- rownames(cor_matrix)[high_cor_pairs[k, 1]]
      col_var <- colnames(cor_matrix)[high_cor_pairs[k, 2]]
      if(col_var %in% colnames(pred)) {
        pred[row_var, col_var] <- 0
        n_zeroed <- n_zeroed + 1
      }
    }
    cat(sprintf("  Zeroed %d high-correlation predictor slots (|r| > 0.95)\n\n", n_zeroed))
  } else {
    cat("  ✓ No near-perfect correlations found\n\n")
  }
}

# ── Remove perfectly correlated redundant predictors identified in Part C ─────
# bzra_weekly_diazepam_eq = bzra_daily_diazepam_eq × 7 (r = 1 by construction).
# Both variables are complete so neither requires imputation, but retaining
# both as predictors causes the VIF singularity and can destabilise imputation
# chains for other variables. The redundant variable's COLUMN is zeroed so it
# is never used to predict any other variable. Its ROW remains as set by
# quickpred() — since it is complete, mice will skip it automatically.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

if(length(redundant_predictors) > 0) {
  cat("Removing perfectly correlated redundant predictors from predictor matrix...\n")
  for(var in redundant_predictors) {
    if(var %in% colnames(pred)) {
      pred[, var] <- 0
      cat(sprintf("  ✓ Zeroed column: %s\n", var))
      cat(sprintf("    (perfectly correlated with another complete variable — r = 1)\n"))
      cat(sprintf("    (not used as a predictor; complete data, so not imputed either)\n"))
    }
  }
  cat("\n")
}

# Report predictor matrix density after quickpred
n_possible  <- nrow(pred) * (ncol(pred) - 1)
n_used      <- sum(pred)
pct_used    <- round(100 * n_used / n_possible, 1)
avg_per_var <- round(n_used / nrow(pred), 1)

cat("PREDICTOR MATRIX SUMMARY (after quickpred):\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat(sprintf("  Possible predictor slots: %d\n", n_possible))
cat(sprintf("  Active predictor slots:   %d (%.1f%%)\n", n_used, pct_used))
cat(sprintf("  Avg predictors per model: %.1f\n", avg_per_var))
if(avg_per_var > 25)
  cat("  ⚠️  Average > 25 — consider raising mincor to 0.25\n")
if(avg_per_var < 5)
  cat("  ⚠️  Average < 5 — mincor may be too high, consider lowering to 0.15\n")
cat("\n")

# ── Remove sparse categorical variables from predictor matrix ─────────────────
# Sparse levels (cell counts < 5) in true factor variables cause perfect
# separation in logreg/polr, producing convergence failures. Zero their column
# so they are never used AS A PREDICTOR. They can still be imputed themselves.
#
# Note: only factor variables reach this point (see Part B3 fix), so no
# numeric Likert items are incorrectly removed here.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("Checking sparse variables flagged in Part B...\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")

if(length(separation_vars) > 0) {
  removed_as_predictors <- character()
  for(var in separation_vars) {
    if(var %in% colnames(pred)) {
      pred[, var] <- 0
      removed_as_predictors <- c(removed_as_predictors, var)
    }
  }
  if(length(removed_as_predictors) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("  Removed %d sparse factor variable(s) as predictors:\n",
                length(removed_as_predictors)))
    for(v in removed_as_predictors)
      cat(sprintf("    • %s\n", v))
    cat("  Note: these variables can still be imputed — they just won't\n")
    cat("        be used to impute others, preventing separation errors.\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("  ✓ No sparse factor variables to remove from predictor matrix\n\n")
}

# Zero out problematic vars (derived, constant, low-n) as predictors
for(var in problematic_vars) {
  if(var %in% colnames(pred)) pred[, var] <- 0
}

prob_in_pred <- problematic_vars[problematic_vars %in% colnames(pred)]
if(length(prob_in_pred) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("  ✓ Problematic variables zeroed as predictors: %s\n\n",
              paste(prob_in_pred, collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  cat("  ✓ No additional problematic variables in predictor matrix\n\n")
}

# Final predictor matrix stats
n_used_final      <- sum(pred)
avg_per_var_final <- round(n_used_final / nrow(pred), 1)
cat(sprintf("FINAL predictor matrix: %d active slots, avg %.1f predictors/model\n\n",
            n_used_final, avg_per_var_final))

# ── Assign imputation methods ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
for(var in continuous_vars)
  if(var %in% names(method) && var %in% vars_with_missing) method[var] <- "pmm"
for(var in binary_vars)
  if(var %in% names(method) && var %in% vars_with_missing) method[var] <- "logreg"
for(var in ordered_vars)
  if(var %in% names(method) && var %in% vars_with_missing) method[var] <- "polr"
for(var in unordered_categorical)
  if(var %in% names(method) && var %in% vars_with_missing) method[var] <- "polyreg"
for(var in problematic_vars)
  if(var %in% names(method)) method[var] <- ""

cat("METHOD SUMMARY:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  PMM:        ", sum(method == "pmm"),     "\n")
cat("  Logreg:     ", sum(method == "logreg"),  "\n")
cat("  Polr:       ", sum(method == "polr"),    "\n")
cat("  Polyreg:    ", sum(method == "polyreg"), "\n")
cat("  Not imputed:", sum(method == ""),        "\n\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART D5: LOGGED EVENTS DIAGNOSTIC & TARGETED REDUCTION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PURPOSE:
#   mice logs events when an imputation model fails or is modified — most
#   commonly due to collinear predictors (singular system), sparse category
#   separation in polr/logreg, or too many predictors relative to observations.
#   Left unaddressed, logged events mean mice is silently dropping predictors
#   or skipping imputations, which biases results and causes non-convergence.
#
# PROCEDURE:
#   1. Run a fast probe imputation (m=1, maxit=5) — cheap, just to surface events
#   2. Parse and categorise every logged event by type
#   3. Apply targeted fixes per event type:
#      a) "system is computationally singular" → the named predictor column
#         is causing linear dependence for that target; zero it in pred
#      b) "perfect predictor" / "rank deficient" → same fix
#      c) polr-specific failures → switch that variable to PMM as fallback
#   4. Re-run probe to verify reduction; report before/after counts
#   5. Pass the cleaned pred + method into all subsequent imputations
#
# NOTE ON ridge:
#   mice() accepts a ridge = <small value> argument that adds a ridge penalty
#   to stabilise near-singular systems without dropping predictors entirely.
#   ridge = 1e-3 is the recommended starting value (van Buuren, 2018 §6.4.2).
#   We apply this as a second-line defence alongside the predictor matrix fixes.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART D5: LOGGED EVENTS DIAGNOSTIC & TARGETED REDUCTION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

# ── Helper: parse loggedEvents into a summary table ──────────────────────────
parse_logged_events <- function(mids_obj) {
  le <- mids_obj$loggedEvents
  if(is.null(le) || nrow(le) == 0) return(NULL)

  # loggedEvents columns: it, im, dep, meth, out
  #   dep  = the target variable being imputed
  #   out  = the predictor variable that caused the problem (may be "")
  #   meth = imputation method used

  le$event_type <- dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("singular|rank.deficient|computationally singular",
          le$out, ignore.case = TRUE)                          ~ "singular_system",
    grepl("perfect predictor",  le$out, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "perfect_predictor",
    grepl("constant",           le$out, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "constant_predictor",
    le$meth %in% c("polr", "polyreg") & le$out != ""          ~ "polr_separation",
    le$meth %in% c("polr", "polyreg") & le$out == ""          ~ "polr_fit_failure",
    le$out != ""                                               ~ "dropped_predictor",
    TRUE                                                       ~ "other"
  )
  le
}

# ── PROBE 1: baseline logged events ──────────────────────────────────────────
cat("PROBE 1: Baseline — running m=1, maxit=5 to surface logged events...\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")

probe1 <- tryCatch(
  mice(df_imp, m = 1, maxit = 5, method = method,
       predictorMatrix = pred, seed = 99, printFlag = FALSE,
       ridge = 1e-3),   # ridge applied from the start as baseline stabiliser
  error = function(e) {
    cat("  ⚠️  Probe failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    NULL
  }
)

n_events_before <- 0L

if(!is.null(probe1)) {

  le1 <- parse_logged_events(probe1)

  if(is.null(le1)) {
    cat("  ✓ No logged events in baseline probe\n\n")
  } else {
    n_events_before <- nrow(le1)
    cat(sprintf("  ⚠️  %d logged events detected\n\n", n_events_before))

    # Summarise by type
    type_summary <- le1 %>%
      dplyr::count(event_type, name = "n") %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n))

    cat("  Event breakdown by type:\n")
    for(r in seq_len(nrow(type_summary)))
      cat(sprintf("    %-30s: %d\n", type_summary$event_type[r], type_summary$n[r]))
    cat("\n")

    # Most affected target variables
    dep_summary <- le1 %>%
      dplyr::count(dep, event_type, name = "n") %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n)) %>%
      head(20)

    cat("  Top affected target variables (dep):\n")
    for(r in seq_len(nrow(dep_summary)))
      cat(sprintf("    %-30s [%-20s]: %d events\n",
                  dep_summary$dep[r], dep_summary$event_type[r], dep_summary$n[r]))
    cat("\n")

    # Most frequently dropped predictors
    out_summary <- le1 %>%
      dplyr::filter(out != "") %>%
      dplyr::count(out, name = "n") %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n)) %>%
      head(20)

    if(nrow(out_summary) > 0) {
      cat("  Most frequently problematic predictors (out):\n")
      for(r in seq_len(nrow(out_summary)))
        cat(sprintf("    %-30s: dropped/flagged %d times\n",
                    out_summary$out[r], out_summary$n[r]))
      cat("\n")
    }

    write.csv(le1, "logged_events_baseline.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    cat("  ✓ Saved: logged_events_baseline.csv\n\n")

    # ── FIX A: Remove problematic predictor columns ─────────────────────────
    # Variables that repeatedly appear in the 'out' column are causing linear
    # dependence in multiple imputation models. Zeroing their COLUMN in pred
    # prevents them being used as predictors.
    #
    # CONTRAST SUFFIX HANDLING:
    # When an ordered factor is used as a predictor in a PMM linear model,
    # R expands it into polynomial contrasts: variable.L (linear), .Q
    # (quadratic), .C (cubic), etc. The 'out' column in loggedEvents contains
    # the contrast name (e.g. "stop_wdl_exp_combined.C"), but the predictor
    # matrix column is named after the original variable ("stop_wdl_exp_combined").
    # We strip known contrast suffixes before looking up the column name.
    # ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    n_fix_a <- 0L

    singular_preds_raw <- le1 %>%
      dplyr::filter(event_type %in% c("singular_system",
                                       "perfect_predictor",
                                       "constant_predictor",
                                       "dropped_predictor")) %>%
      dplyr::filter(out != "") %>%
      dplyr::count(out, name = "n") %>%
      dplyr::filter(n >= 3) %>%
      dplyr::pull(out)

    # Strip polynomial contrast suffixes (.L, .Q, .C, .^4, .^5 etc.)
    singular_preds <- unique(
      sub("\\.(L|Q|C|(\\^[0-9]+))$", "", singular_preds_raw)
    )

    if(length(singular_preds) > 0) {
      cat("  FIX A: Zeroing frequently-problematic predictor columns\n")
      cat("         (flagged ≥ 3 times; contrast suffixes stripped for lookup)\n")
      for(var in singular_preds) {
        if(var %in% colnames(pred)) {
          pred[, var] <- 0
          n_fix_a <- n_fix_a + 1L
          # Report original flagged name alongside the column zeroed
          flagged_as <- singular_preds_raw[sub("\\.(L|Q|C|(\\^[0-9]+))$", "",
                                               singular_preds_raw) == var]
          cat(sprintf("    ✓ Zeroed column: %-30s  (flagged as: %s)\n",
                      var, paste(unique(flagged_as), collapse = ", ")))
        }
      }
      cat("\n")
    } else {
      cat("  FIX A: No columns meet the ≥ 3 events threshold — no zeroing applied\n\n")
    }

    # ── FIX B: Switch polr failures to PMM ──────────────────────────────────
    # polr (ordered logistic regression) is the most fragile mice method.
    # When a polr model fails to fit (separation, insufficient variation),
    # mice logs an event and produces poor imputations. Switching those
    # specific variables to PMM is a valid and common fallback:
    #   - PMM is more robust and non-parametric
    #   - Ordinal structure is approximately preserved by matching observed donors
    #   - Van Buuren (2018) endorses PMM as fallback for problematic ordered vars
    # ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    polr_failures <- le1 %>%
      dplyr::filter(event_type %in% c("polr_fit_failure", "polr_separation")) %>%
      dplyr::pull(dep) %>%
      unique()

    n_fix_b <- 0L

    if(length(polr_failures) > 0) {
      cat("  FIX B: Switching repeatedly-failing polr variables to PMM\n")
      cat("         (polr fit failure / separation detected in probe)\n")
      for(var in polr_failures) {
        if(var %in% names(method) && method[var] == "polr") {
          method[var] <- "pmm"
          n_fix_b <- n_fix_b + 1L
          cat(sprintf("    ✓ %s: polr → pmm\n", var))
        }
      }
      cat("\n")
    } else {
      cat("  FIX B: No polr-specific failures detected\n\n")
    }

    # ── PROBE 2: verify improvement ─────────────────────────────────────────
    if(n_fix_a > 0 || n_fix_b > 0) {

      cat("  PROBE 2: Re-running after fixes to verify improvement...\n")

      probe2 <- tryCatch(
        mice(df_imp, m = 1, maxit = 5, method = method,
             predictorMatrix = pred, seed = 99, printFlag = FALSE,
             ridge = 1e-3),
        error = function(e) {
          cat("  ⚠️  Probe 2 failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
          NULL
        }
      )

      if(!is.null(probe2)) {
        le2 <- parse_logged_events(probe2)
        n_events_after <- if(is.null(le2)) 0L else nrow(le2)

        cat(sprintf("\n  LOGGED EVENTS: %d → %d  (reduction: %d, %.0f%%)\n\n",
                    n_events_before, n_events_after,
                    n_events_before - n_events_after,
                    100 * (n_events_before - n_events_after) / max(n_events_before, 1)))

        if(!is.null(le2) && nrow(le2) > 0) {
          cat("  Remaining events after fixes:\n")
          remaining_types <- le2 %>%
            dplyr::count(event_type, name = "n") %>%
            dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n))
          for(r in seq_len(nrow(remaining_types)))
            cat(sprintf("    %-30s: %d\n",
                        remaining_types$event_type[r], remaining_types$n[r]))
          cat("\n")
          write.csv(le2, "logged_events_after_fixes.csv", row.names = FALSE)
          cat("  ✓ Saved: logged_events_after_fixes.csv\n\n")
        }
      }

    } else {
      cat("  ℹ️  No structural fixes applied (ridge = 1e-3 is the active stabiliser)\n\n")
    }
  }

} else {
  cat("  ℹ️  Probe skipped — will apply ridge = 1e-3 in all imputations\n\n")
}

# ── Update final predictor matrix stats after D5 fixes ───────────────────────
n_used_final      <- sum(pred)
avg_per_var_final <- round(n_used_final / nrow(pred), 1)

cat("UPDATED METHOD SUMMARY (after D5 fixes):\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  PMM:        ", sum(method == "pmm"),     "\n")
cat("  Logreg:     ", sum(method == "logreg"),  "\n")
cat("  Polr:       ", sum(method == "polr"),    "\n")
cat("  Polyreg:    ", sum(method == "polyreg"), "\n")
cat("  Not imputed:", sum(method == ""),        "\n")
cat(sprintf("  Predictor matrix: %d active slots, avg %.1f/model\n\n",
            n_used_final, avg_per_var_final))

cat("NOTE: ridge = 1e-3 will be applied in all subsequent mice() calls.\n")
cat("  This adds a small ridge penalty to stabilise near-singular systems\n")
cat("  (van Buuren, 2018 §6.4.2). Results are minimally affected at this value.\n\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART E: STATISTICAL DERIVATION OF m — VON HIPPEL (2020) TWO-STAGE PROCEDURE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART E: STATISTICAL DERIVATION OF m (NUMBER OF IMPUTATIONS)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

cat("METHOD: Von Hippel (2020) two-stage FMI-based quadratic rule\n")
cat("  Citation: Von Hippel, P.T. (2020). How many imputations do you\n")
cat("  need? A two-stage calculation using a quadratic rule.\n")
cat("  Sociological Methods & Research, 49(3), 699-718.\n")
cat("  DOI: 10.1177/0049124117747303\n\n")

cat("RATIONALE:\n")
cat("  The required number of imputations is not fixed — it depends on\n")
cat("  the Fraction of Missing Information (FMI) in your specific data.\n")
cat("  FMI is not the fraction of missing values; it is the fraction by\n")
cat("  which the squared standard error would shrink if data were complete.\n")
cat("  Von Hippel (2020) shows that m scales quadratically with FMI:\n")
cat("  m = 1 + 200 * FMI^2  (for CV(SE) = 0.05, i.e., 5% replicability)\n\n")

cat("STAGE 1: Pilot imputation with m = 20 to estimate FMI\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  Running pilot imputation (m=20, maxit=20)...\n")

pilot_imp <- tryCatch({
  mice(df_imp, m = 20, maxit = 20, method = method,
       predictorMatrix = pred, seed = 12345, printFlag = FALSE,
       ridge = 1e-3)
}, error = function(e) {
  cat("  ⚠️  Pilot imputation failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  NULL
})

if(!is.null(pilot_imp)) {
  cat("  ✓ Pilot imputation complete\n\n")

  max_miss_var <- names(which.max(missing_pct))
  max_miss_pct <- max(missing_pct)

  cat("STAGE 2: Estimating FMI from pilot imputations\n")
  cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
  cat("  Variable used for FMI estimation:", max_miss_var,
      "(highest missingness:", round(max_miss_pct, 1), "%)\n")
  cat("  Note: FMI from highest-missing variable gives conservative (safe) m\n\n")

  available_preds <- names(df_imp)[
    names(df_imp) != max_miss_var &
    sapply(df_imp, is.numeric) &
    colSums(is.na(df_imp)) == 0
  ]
  available_preds <- head(available_preds, 10)

  fmi_result <- tryCatch({
    if(length(available_preds) >= 2) {

      fmi_formula <- as.formula(paste(max_miss_var, "~",
                                      paste(available_preds, collapse = " + ")))

      cat("  Fitting model across", pilot_imp$m, "imputed datasets...\n")

      fits <- lapply(1:pilot_imp$m, function(i) {
        completed_data <- mice::complete(pilot_imp, action = i)
        lm(fmi_formula, data = completed_data)
      })

      pooled_fit <- mice::pool(as.mira(fits))
      cat("  ✓ Model pooled across imputations\n\n")

      fmi_m              <- how_many_imputations(pooled_fit)
      fmi_m_conservative <- how_many_imputations(pooled_fit, cv = 0.01)

      list(m_standard = fmi_m, m_conservative = fmi_m_conservative, success = TRUE)

    } else {
      cat("  ⚠️  Insufficient complete numeric predictors for FMI model\n")
      cat("      (need ≥ 2, found", length(available_preds), ")\n")
      list(success = FALSE)
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("  ⚠️  FMI calculation failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    list(success = FALSE)
  })

  if(isTRUE(fmi_result$success)) {
    cat("FMI-BASED m CALCULATION:\n")
    cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
    cat(sprintf("  m for CV(SE) = 0.05 (5%% precision):  %d imputations\n",
                fmi_result$m_standard))
    cat(sprintf("  m for CV(SE) = 0.01 (1%% precision):  %d imputations\n",
                fmi_result$m_conservative))
    cat("\n")

    m_white_floor <- ceiling(max_miss_pct)
    m_vonhippel   <- fmi_result$m_standard
    optimal_m     <- max(m_vonhippel, m_white_floor, 20)

    if(optimal_m > 100) {
      cat(sprintf("  Initial calculation: %d (capped at 100 for feasibility)\n", optimal_m))
      optimal_m <- 100
    }

    cat("DECISION:\n")
    cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
    cat(sprintf("  Von Hippel (2020) quadratic rule:    m = %d\n", m_vonhippel))
    cat(sprintf("  White et al. (2011) floor (≥%% miss): m = %d\n", m_white_floor))
    cat(sprintf("  Minimum recommended:                 m = 20\n"))
    cat(sprintf("  → SELECTED m = %d\n\n", optimal_m))

    cat("JUSTIFICATION FOR MANUSCRIPT:\n")
    cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
    cat(sprintf(
      "  The number of imputations (m = %d) was determined using the\n", optimal_m))
    cat("  Von Hippel (2020) two-stage quadratic rule. A pilot imputation\n")
    cat("  with m = 20 was conducted to estimate the Fraction of Missing\n")
    cat("  Information (FMI). FMI — the fraction by which the squared\n")
    cat("  standard error would shrink with complete data — was estimated\n")
    cat(sprintf("  from the variable with the most missing data (%s, %.1f%%).\n",
                max_miss_var, max_miss_pct))
    cat("  The FMI-based quadratic formula (m = 1 + 200×FMI²) indicated\n")
    cat(sprintf("  m = %d imputations for 5%% replicability of standard errors.\n",
                m_vonhippel))
    cat("  This was compared against the White et al. (2011) floor\n")
    cat(sprintf("  of m ≥ %d (≥ %% missing data), and the final m = %d\n",
                m_white_floor, optimal_m))
    cat("  was selected as the maximum of these criteria.\n\n")

  } else {
    cat("Falling back to White et al. (2011) missingness-based rule\n\n")
    max_miss_pct  <- max(missing_pct)
    m_white_floor <- ceiling(max_miss_pct)
    optimal_m     <- max(m_white_floor, 20)
    if(optimal_m > 100) optimal_m <- 100

    cat("DECISION:\n")
    cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
    cat(sprintf("  White et al. (2011) rule (m ≥ %% missing): m = %d\n", m_white_floor))
    cat(sprintf("  Minimum recommended:                       m = 20\n"))
    cat(sprintf("  → SELECTED m = %d\n\n", optimal_m))
  }

} else {
  cat("  Pilot imputation failed — falling back to missingness-based approach\n\n")
  max_miss_pct  <- max(missing_pct)
  m_white_floor <- ceiling(max_miss_pct)
  optimal_m     <- max(m_white_floor, 20)
  if(optimal_m > 100) optimal_m <- 100
  cat(sprintf("  → SELECTED m = %d (White et al., 2011)\n\n", optimal_m))
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART F: EMPIRICAL MAXIT DETERMINATION — CONVERGENCE EXPERIMENT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RATIONALE:
#   maxit controls Markov chain length in MICE's chained equations algorithm.
#   Unlike m, it cannot be derived mathematically — it must be diagnosed
#   empirically (van Buuren, 2018; Gelman & Rubin, 1992).
#
#   PROCEDURE:
#     1. Run small pilot (m=5) at maxit = 10, 20, 30, 40
#     2. Assess Gelman-Rubin PSRF < 1.1 at each step
#     3. Select smallest maxit where convergence is confirmed
#
#   Using m=5 is valid because convergence behaviour is independent of m.
#   This keeps experimentation fast before the final large imputation.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART F: EMPIRICAL MAXIT DETERMINATION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

cat("METHOD: Structured convergence experiment\n")
cat("  • Pilot m = 5 (convergence behaviour is independent of m)\n")
cat("  • Test maxit = 10, 20, 30, 40\n")
cat("  • Convergence criterion: Gelman-Rubin PSRF < 1.1 for all variables\n")
cat("  • Select smallest maxit achieving convergence\n\n")

cat("CITATIONS:\n")
cat("  • van Buuren (2018): maxit determined empirically via trace plots\n")
cat("  • Gelman & Rubin (1992): PSRF < 1.1 as convergence threshold\n")
cat("  • Brooks & Gelman (1998): general MCMC convergence monitoring\n\n")

maxit_candidates <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)
convergence_results <- data.frame(
  maxit       = maxit_candidates,
  max_psrf    = NA_real_,
  mean_psrf   = NA_real_,
  n_above_1.1 = NA_integer_,
  converged   = NA,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cat("Running convergence experiment (m=5 for each candidate)...\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")

pilot_imps <- list()

for(i in seq_along(maxit_candidates)) {

  maxit_test <- maxit_candidates[i]
  cat(sprintf("Testing maxit = %d ...\n", maxit_test))

  pilot_imp_test <- tryCatch({
    mice(df_imp, m = 5, maxit = maxit_test, method = method,
         predictorMatrix = pred, seed = 12345, printFlag = FALSE,
         ridge = 1e-3)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("  ⚠️  Imputation failed: %s\n", conditionMessage(e)))
    NULL
  })

  if(!is.null(pilot_imp_test)) {
    pilot_imps[[as.character(maxit_test)]] <- pilot_imp_test

    # ── Compute PSRF directly from mids$chainMean ────────────────────────────
    # mice::convergence(diagnostic = "gr") stacks all iterations into one
    # data frame with no reliable iteration label in some mice versions.
    #
    # We use mids$chainMean directly — a 3-D array [n_imputed_vars, maxit, m].
    # The m chains are treated as parallel MCMC chains and PSRF is computed
    # at the FINAL iteration only using coda::gelman.diag().
    #
    # IMPORTANT — why we do NOT use <<- inside tryCatch:
    # <<- inside a tryCatch body searches the enclosing call stack, which is
    # unreliable when scripts are sourced or run inside knitr/RMarkdown chunks
    # (each chunk runs in its own environment). Instead we return computed
    # values as a named list and assign to convergence_results OUTSIDE the
    # tryCatch, where the assignment is always in the correct frame.
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    psrf_result <- tryCatch({

      if(!requireNamespace("coda", quietly = TRUE))
        stop("coda package required — install with: install.packages('coda')")

      cm <- pilot_imp_test$chainMean  # [n_vars, maxit, m]

      if(is.null(cm) || length(dim(cm)) != 3)
        stop("chainMean has unexpected structure")

      n_imp_vars <- dim(cm)[1]
      n_iter     <- dim(cm)[2]
      n_chains   <- dim(cm)[3]

      cat(sprintf("  Computing PSRF from chainMean [%d vars × %d iters × %d chains]...\n",
                  n_imp_vars, n_iter, n_chains))

      if(n_chains < 2)
        stop("Need m ≥ 2 chains for Gelman-Rubin (m=5 used here, so this should not occur)")

      psrf_vec <- numeric(n_imp_vars)

      for(v in seq_len(n_imp_vars)) {

        chain_list <- lapply(seq_len(n_chains), function(j) {
          vals <- cm[v, , j]
          if(all(is.na(vals)) || var(vals, na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-15) return(NULL)
          coda::mcmc(vals)
        })
        chain_list <- Filter(Negate(is.null), chain_list)

        if(length(chain_list) < 2) {
          psrf_vec[v] <- 1.0   # constant chain = converged by definition
          next
        }

        gd <- tryCatch(
          coda::gelman.diag(coda::mcmc.list(chain_list),
                            autoburnin = FALSE,
                            multivariate = FALSE),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )

        psrf_vec[v] <- if(!is.null(gd)) gd$psrf[1, 1] else NA_real_
      }

      psrf_vec  <- psrf_vec[!is.na(psrf_vec) & is.finite(psrf_vec)]
      max_psrf  <- max(psrf_vec)
      mean_psrf <- mean(psrf_vec)
      n_above   <- sum(psrf_vec > 1.1)
      converged <- max_psrf < 1.1

      list(success   = TRUE,
           max_psrf  = round(max_psrf,  4),
           mean_psrf = round(mean_psrf, 4),
           n_above   = n_above,
           n_vars    = length(psrf_vec),
           converged = converged)

    }, error = function(e) {
      list(success = FALSE, error_msg = conditionMessage(e))
    })

    # ── Assign results outside tryCatch — safe in all execution contexts ──────
    if(isTRUE(psrf_result$success)) {

      convergence_results$max_psrf[i]    <- psrf_result$max_psrf
      convergence_results$mean_psrf[i]   <- psrf_result$mean_psrf
      convergence_results$n_above_1.1[i] <- psrf_result$n_above
      convergence_results$converged[i]   <- psrf_result$converged

      status <- if(psrf_result$converged) "✓ CONVERGED" else "✗ NOT CONVERGED"
      cat(sprintf("  %s | Max PSRF = %.4f | Mean PSRF = %.4f | N > 1.1: %d / %d\n",
                  status, psrf_result$max_psrf, psrf_result$mean_psrf,
                  psrf_result$n_above, psrf_result$n_vars))

    } else {
      cat(sprintf("  ⚠️  PSRF calculation failed: %s\n", psrf_result$error_msg))
      n_warnings <- if(!is.null(pilot_imp_test$loggedEvents))
                      nrow(pilot_imp_test$loggedEvents) else 0
      cat(sprintf("      Falling back to logged events: %d\n", n_warnings))
      convergence_results$converged[i] <- (n_warnings == 0)
    }

  } else {
    cat("  ✗ FAILED\n")
  }
  cat("\n")
}

# Select optimal maxit
cat("CONVERGENCE EXPERIMENT RESULTS:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
print(convergence_results[, c("maxit", "max_psrf", "mean_psrf",
                               "n_above_1.1", "converged")],
      row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n")

converged_rows <- convergence_results[
  !is.na(convergence_results$converged) & convergence_results$converged == TRUE, ]

if(nrow(converged_rows) > 0) {
  optimal_maxit <- min(converged_rows$maxit)
  cat(sprintf("✓ Convergence first achieved at maxit = %d\n", optimal_maxit))

  if(nrow(converged_rows) > 1) {
    psrf_at_optimal <- converged_rows$max_psrf[converged_rows$maxit == optimal_maxit]
    psrf_at_max     <- converged_rows$max_psrf[which.max(converged_rows$maxit)]
    psrf_change     <- abs(psrf_at_optimal - psrf_at_max)
    cat(sprintf("  Max PSRF at maxit=%d: %.4f\n", optimal_maxit, psrf_at_optimal))
    cat(sprintf("  Max PSRF at maxit=%d: %.4f\n",
                max(converged_rows$maxit), psrf_at_max))
    cat(sprintf("  Difference:           %.4f\n", psrf_change))
    if(psrf_change < 0.01)
      cat("  ✓ Higher maxit shows negligible improvement — selected value is sufficient\n")
  }

} else {
  cat("⚠️  No tested maxit value achieved full convergence\n")
  cat("    Using maxit = 40 as best available option\n")
  cat("    Consider reviewing logged events and VIF results\n")
  optimal_maxit <- 40
}

cat(sprintf("\n→ SELECTED maxit = %d\n\n", optimal_maxit))

# Save trace plots for selected maxit
selected_pilot <- pilot_imps[[as.character(optimal_maxit)]]
if(!is.null(selected_pilot)) {
  tryCatch({
    pdf("convergence_trace_plots_pilot.pdf", width = 12, height = 8)
    plot(selected_pilot,
         main = paste0("Pilot Trace Plots — maxit = ", optimal_maxit, " (m=5)"))
    dev.off()
    cat("✓ Saved: convergence_trace_plots_pilot.pdf\n")
    cat("  → Review: chains should intermingle freely with no directional trend\n\n")
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("  ⚠️  Could not save trace plots:", conditionMessage(e), "\n\n")
  })
}

write.csv(convergence_results, "convergence_experiment_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("✓ Saved: convergence_experiment_results.csv\n\n")

cat("JUSTIFICATION FOR MANUSCRIPT:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat(sprintf(
  "  The number of iterations (maxit = %d) was determined empirically\n",
  optimal_maxit))
cat("  using a structured convergence experiment. Pilot imputations\n")
cat("  with m = 5 were run at maxit = 10, 20, 30, and 40. At each\n")
cat("  step, convergence was assessed using the Gelman-Rubin Potential\n")
cat("  Scale Reduction Factor (PSRF; Gelman & Rubin, 1992; Brooks &\n")
cat("  Gelman, 1998), with PSRF < 1.1 as the convergence threshold.\n")
cat(sprintf("  Convergence was first achieved at maxit = %d, with higher\n",
            optimal_maxit))
cat("  values producing negligible further improvement. Trace plots\n")
cat("  confirmed freely intermingling chains with no directional\n")
cat(sprintf("  trends (van Buuren, 2018). Final imputation used maxit = %d.\n\n",
            optimal_maxit))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART G: SAVE OPTIMIZATION RESULTS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART G: SAVING OPTIMIZATION RESULTS\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

saveRDS(df_imp, "df_imputation_ready.rds")
cat("✓ Saved: df_imputation_ready.rds\n")

imputation_parameters <- list(
  optimal_m = optimal_m,
  optimal_m_justification = paste0(
    "Von Hippel (2020) two-stage FMI quadratic rule. ",
    "Pilot m=20. FMI estimated from highest-missing variable (",
    names(which.max(missing_pct)), ", ", round(max(missing_pct), 1), "% missing). ",
    "Floor: White et al. (2011) m >= % missing = ", ceiling(max(missing_pct)), "."
  ),
  optimal_maxit = optimal_maxit,
  optimal_maxit_justification = paste0(
    "Empirical convergence experiment: m=5 pilot at maxit=10,20,30,40. ",
    "Gelman-Rubin PSRF < 1.1 criterion (Gelman & Rubin, 1992). ",
    "Convergence first achieved at maxit=", optimal_maxit, "."
  ),
  convergence_experiment  = convergence_results,
  method                  = method,
  predictor_matrix        = pred,
  variable_types = list(
    continuous  = continuous_vars,
    binary      = binary_vars,
    ordered     = ordered_vars,
    unordered   = unordered_categorical
  ),
  excluded_variables               = c(outcome, problematic_vars),
  derived_variables_to_recalculate = derived_vars,
  redundant_predictors_zeroed      = redundant_predictors,
  ridge_penalty                    = 1e-3,
  logged_events_before_fixes       = n_events_before,
  n_observations      = nrow(df_imp),
  n_variables         = ncol(df_imp),
  n_vars_to_impute    = sum(method != ""),
  max_missingness_pct = max(missing_pct),
  avg_missingness_pct = mean(missing_pct[missing_pct > 0]),
  reverse_coding_done = list(
    bfi   = analysis_vars$bfi_reversed,
    surps = analysis_vars$surps_reversed
  )
)

saveRDS(imputation_parameters, "imputation_parameters_optimized.rds")
cat("✓ Saved: imputation_parameters_optimized.rds\n\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART H: FINAL SUMMARY
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("DIAGNOSTICS COMPLETE — SUMMARY\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

cat("STATISTICALLY-DERIVED PARAMETERS:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat(sprintf("  m     = %d  (Von Hippel, 2020 FMI quadratic rule)\n", optimal_m))
cat(sprintf("  maxit = %d  (empirical PSRF convergence experiment)\n", optimal_maxit))
cat(sprintf("  Variables to impute: %d\n", sum(method != "")))
cat(sprintf("  Observations:        %d\n\n", nrow(df_imp)))

cat("IMPUTATION METHOD BREAKDOWN:\n")
cat(sprintf("  PMM (continuous):           %d\n", sum(method == "pmm")))
cat(sprintf("  Logreg (binary):            %d\n", sum(method == "logreg")))
cat(sprintf("  Polr (ordered):             %d\n", sum(method == "polr")))
cat(sprintf("  Polyreg (unordered):        %d\n", sum(method == "polyreg")))
cat(sprintf("  Not imputed:                %d\n\n", sum(method == "")))

cat("PREDICTOR MATRIX:\n")
cat(sprintf("  mincor used:                0.10\n"))
cat(sprintf("  minpuc used:                0.10 (excludes block-missing within-scale pairs)\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Final avg predictors/model: %.1f\n\n", avg_per_var_final))

cat("SCALE ITEMS FORCED TO NUMERIC:\n")
cat(sprintf("  DBAS (%d), BFI (%d), SURPS (%d), CISS (%d) → integer/PMM\n\n",
            sum(analysis_vars$dbas  %in% scale_vars_all),
            sum(analysis_vars$bfi   %in% scale_vars_all),
            sum(analysis_vars$surps %in% scale_vars_all),
            sum(analysis_vars$ciss  %in% scale_vars_all)))

cat("BZRA DOSE VARIABLES:\n")
for(v in c("bzra_daily_diazepam_eq", "bzra_weekly_diazepam_eq"))
  cat(sprintf("  %-30s: %s\n", v,
              if(v %in% continuous_vars) "PMM (continuous)" else "⚠️ Not assigned"))
cat("\n")

cat("LOGGED EVENTS REDUCTION (Part D5):\n")
cat(sprintf("  ridge penalty applied:          1e-3 (all mice calls)\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Baseline logged events (probe): %d\n", n_events_before))
cat(sprintf("  Fix A — predictor columns zeroed based on events\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Fix B — polr failures switched to PMM\n\n"))

if(length(redundant_predictors) > 0) {
  cat("PERFECTLY CORRELATED PREDICTORS ZEROED (Part C + predictor matrix):\n")
  for(v in redundant_predictors)
    cat(sprintf("  • %s (column zeroed — r = 1 with another complete variable)\n", v))
  cat("\n")
}

cat("CONVERGENCE EXPERIMENT SUMMARY:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
print(convergence_results[, c("maxit", "max_psrf", "mean_psrf",
                               "n_above_1.1", "converged")],
      row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\n  → Convergence first achieved at maxit = %d\n\n", optimal_maxit))

cat("KEY CITATIONS:\n")
cat("  • Von Hippel (2020) Sociol Methods Res 49(3):699-718  [m]\n")
cat("  • White et al. (2011) Stat Med 30(4):377-399          [m floor]\n")
cat("  • Gelman & Rubin (1992) Stat Sci 7(4):457-472         [maxit]\n")
cat("  • Brooks & Gelman (1998) J Comp Graph Stat 7(4):434   [maxit]\n")
cat("  • Van Buuren (2018) Flexible Imputation (2nd ed.)      [both]\n\n")

if(length(problematic_vars) > 0) {
  cat("EXCLUDED/ADJUSTED VARIABLES:\n")
  cat("  • Outcome excluded:", outcome, "\n")
  cat("  • Derived (recalculate post-imputation):",
      paste(derived_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  other_prob <- setdiff(problematic_vars, derived_vars)
  if(length(other_prob) > 0)
    cat("  • Other problematic:", paste(other_prob, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("\n")
}

cat("FILES CREATED:\n")
cat("  1. df_imputation_ready.rds               - Dataset ready for imputation\n")
cat("  2. imputation_parameters_optimized.rds   - Parameters + citations\n")
cat("  3. pre_imputation_missingness_summary.csv\n")
cat("  4. convergence_experiment_results.csv    - PSRF at each maxit tested\n")
cat("  5. convergence_trace_plots_pilot.pdf     - Trace plots for selected maxit\n")
cat("  6. logged_events_baseline.csv            - Raw logged events before fixes\n")
cat("  7. logged_events_after_fixes.csv         - Remaining events after D5 fixes\n")
if(file.exists("vif_analysis.csv"))
  cat("  8. vif_analysis.csv\n")
cat("\n")

cat("NEXT STEP: Proceed to Chunk 8 (Multiple Imputation)\n\n")

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("✓ PRE-IMPUTATION DIAGNOSTICS COMPLETE\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")
```





## Multiple Imputation
```{r}
#==============================================================================
# CHUNK 8: MULTIPLE IMPUTATION
#==============================================================================
# Purpose: Perform multiple imputation using MICE with parameters optimized
#          in Chunk 7, then run comprehensive statistical verification
# Outputs: Imputed datasets + full diagnostic report
#
# CHUNK 7 PARAMETERS CARRIED FORWARD:
#   ridge = 1e-3              (stability stabiliser, van Buuren §6.4.2)
#   mincor = 0.10, minpuc = 0.10  (predictor matrix)
#   stop_wdl_exp_combined     (zeroed as predictor — cubic contrast singularity)
#   6 polr vars → PMM         (Fix B switches from Chunk 7 D5)
#   bzra_weekly_diazepam_eq   (zeroed as predictor — r = 1 with daily)
#==============================================================================

library(mice)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(coda)

cat("\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("MULTIPLE IMPUTATION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

# Load optimized parameters from Chunk 7
if(!file.exists("df_imputation_ready.rds") || !file.exists("imputation_parameters_optimized.rds")) {
  stop("ERROR: Required files not found. Please run Chunk 7 first.")
}

df_imp     <- readRDS("df_imputation_ready.rds")
imp_params <- readRDS("imputation_parameters_optimized.rds")

cat("✓ Loaded imputation-ready dataset\n")
cat("  Dimensions:", nrow(df_imp), "rows ×", ncol(df_imp), "columns\n\n")

cat("✓ Loaded optimized parameters from Chunk 7\n")
cat("  m     =", imp_params$optimal_m, "\n")
cat("  maxit =", imp_params$optimal_maxit, "\n")
cat("  ridge =", imp_params$ridge_penalty, "\n")
cat("  Variables to impute:", imp_params$n_vars_to_impute, "\n\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART A: RUNNING MULTIPLE IMPUTATION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART A: RUNNING MULTIPLE IMPUTATION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

cat("IMPUTATION PARAMETERS:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  Number of imputations (m):", imp_params$optimal_m, "\n")
cat("  Iterations (maxit):       ", imp_params$optimal_maxit, "\n")
cat("  Ridge penalty:            ", imp_params$ridge_penalty, "\n")
cat("  Variables to impute:      ", imp_params$n_vars_to_impute, "\n")
cat("  Imputation methods:\n")
cat("    • PMM:    ", sum(imp_params$method == "pmm"),     "variables\n")
cat("    • Logreg: ", sum(imp_params$method == "logreg"),  "variables\n")
cat("    • Polr:   ", sum(imp_params$method == "polr"),    "variables\n")
cat("    • Polyreg:", sum(imp_params$method == "polyreg"), "variables\n\n")

cat("JUSTIFICATION:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  m:     ", imp_params$optimal_m_justification,    "\n\n")
cat("  maxit: ", imp_params$optimal_maxit_justification, "\n\n")

cat("CHUNK 7 ADJUSTMENTS APPLIED:\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")

if(!is.null(imp_params$redundant_predictors_zeroed) &&
   length(imp_params$redundant_predictors_zeroed) > 0) {
  for(v in imp_params$redundant_predictors_zeroed)
    cat(sprintf("  • %-35s zeroed as predictor (r = 1)\n", v))
}

# Report polr → PMM switches (method has "pmm" for vars originally polr)
polr_to_pmm <- names(imp_params$method)[imp_params$method == "pmm" &
  names(imp_params$method) %in% imp_params$variable_types$ordered]
if(length(polr_to_pmm) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("  • %d ordered vars switched polr → PMM (Fix B, Chunk 7 D5):\n",
              length(polr_to_pmm)))
  for(v in polr_to_pmm) cat(sprintf("      %s\n", v))
}
cat("\n")

# Run MICE
cat("Starting imputation...\n")
cat("This may take several minutes...\n\n")

start_time <- Sys.time()

imp_final <- mice(
  data             = df_imp,
  m                = imp_params$optimal_m,
  maxit            = imp_params$optimal_maxit,
  method           = imp_params$method,
  predictorMatrix  = imp_params$predictor_matrix,
  ridge            = imp_params$ridge_penalty,
  seed             = 12345,
  printFlag        = TRUE
)

end_time     <- Sys.time()
elapsed_time <- difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "mins")

cat("\n✓ Imputation complete!\n")
cat("  Time elapsed:", round(as.numeric(elapsed_time), 2), "minutes\n\n")

# Logged events check (safe NULL handling)
n_logged <- if(!is.null(imp_final$loggedEvents)) nrow(imp_final$loggedEvents) else 0L

if(n_logged > 0) {
  cat("⚠️  LOGGED EVENTS DURING FINAL IMPUTATION:\n")
  cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
  cat("  Total events:", n_logged, "\n")
  event_summary <- table(imp_final$loggedEvents$out)
  cat("  Event types:\n")
  for(event in names(event_summary))
    cat("    •", event, ":", event_summary[event], "times\n")
  cat("\n  First 10 events:\n")
  print(head(imp_final$loggedEvents, 10))
  write.csv(imp_final$loggedEvents, "imputation_logged_events.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  cat("  ✓ Saved: imputation_logged_events.csv\n\n")
} else {
  cat("✓ No logged events — imputation completed without issues\n\n")
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART B: CONVERGENCE DIAGNOSTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART B: CONVERGENCE DIAGNOSTICS\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

# ── B1. Gelman-Rubin PSRF on final imputation chains ─────────────────────────
# Mirrors the exact procedure from Chunk 7 Part F, now applied to the full
# m = optimal_m run. PSRF < 1.1 for all variables confirms the final
# imputation has converged, not just the pilot.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("B1. Gelman-Rubin PSRF on final imputation\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  Computing PSRF from chainMean [vars × maxit × m]...\n")

psrf_final <- tryCatch({

  cm         <- imp_final$chainMean
  n_imp_vars <- dim(cm)[1]
  n_iter     <- dim(cm)[2]
  n_chains   <- dim(cm)[3]

  psrf_vec  <- numeric(n_imp_vars)
  var_names <- dimnames(cm)[[1]]

  for(v in seq_len(n_imp_vars)) {
    chain_list <- lapply(seq_len(n_chains), function(j) {
      vals <- cm[v, , j]
      if(all(is.na(vals)) || var(vals, na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-15) return(NULL)
      coda::mcmc(vals)
    })
    chain_list <- Filter(Negate(is.null), chain_list)
    if(length(chain_list) < 2) { psrf_vec[v] <- 1.0; next }
    gd <- tryCatch(
      coda::gelman.diag(coda::mcmc.list(chain_list),
                        autoburnin = FALSE, multivariate = FALSE),
      error = function(e) NULL)
    psrf_vec[v] <- if(!is.null(gd)) gd$psrf[1, 1] else NA_real_
  }

  psrf_vec <- setNames(psrf_vec, var_names)
  psrf_vec

}, error = function(e) {
  cat("  ⚠️  PSRF calculation failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  NULL
})

if(!is.null(psrf_final)) {
  psrf_clean <- psrf_final[!is.na(psrf_final) & is.finite(psrf_final)]
  max_psrf   <- max(psrf_clean)
  mean_psrf  <- mean(psrf_clean)
  n_above    <- sum(psrf_clean > 1.1)
  converged  <- max_psrf < 1.1

  cat(sprintf("  Max PSRF:    %.4f %s\n", max_psrf,
              if(max_psrf < 1.1) "✓" else "⚠️"))
  cat(sprintf("  Mean PSRF:   %.4f\n", mean_psrf))
  cat(sprintf("  N > 1.1:     %d / %d\n", n_above, length(psrf_clean)))

  if(converged) {
    cat("  ✓ CONVERGED — all chains settled (PSRF < 1.1)\n\n")
  } else {
    cat("  ⚠️  NOT FULLY CONVERGED — consider increasing maxit\n\n")
    cat("  Variables with PSRF > 1.1:\n")
    high_psrf_vars <- sort(psrf_clean[psrf_clean > 1.1], decreasing = TRUE)
    for(v in seq_along(high_psrf_vars))
      cat(sprintf("    %2d. %-35s PSRF = %.4f\n",
                  v, names(high_psrf_vars)[v], high_psrf_vars[v]))
    cat("\n")
  }

  psrf_df <- data.frame(
    variable = names(psrf_clean),
    psrf     = round(psrf_clean, 4),
    converged = psrf_clean < 1.1
  ) %>% arrange(desc(psrf))

  write.csv(psrf_df, "final_imputation_psrf.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  cat("  ✓ Saved: final_imputation_psrf.csv\n\n")
}

# ── B2. Trace plots ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("B2. Trace plots\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")

vars_to_plot <- c(
  "age", "education", "income",
  "phq2_score", "osss_3_score", "med_quant",
  "ciss11", "ciss21", "surps17", "surps23_r",
  "side_effects_1", "safety_1", "dependence_1",
  "motivation_1", "desires_1", "capability"
)
vars_to_plot <- vars_to_plot[
  vars_to_plot %in% names(imp_params$method[imp_params$method != ""])]

cat("  Plotting", length(vars_to_plot), "representative variables...\n")
tryCatch({
  pdf("convergence_trace_plots_final.pdf", width = 14, height = 10)
  plot(imp_final, y = vars_to_plot,
       main = paste0("Final Imputation Trace Plots (m=",
                     imp_params$optimal_m, ", maxit=",
                     imp_params$optimal_maxit, ")"))
  dev.off()
  cat("  ✓ Saved: convergence_trace_plots_final.pdf\n")
  cat("    → Chains should intermingle freely with no directional trends\n\n")
}, error = function(e)
  cat("  ⚠️  Trace plot failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n\n"))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART C: DISTRIBUTION DIAGNOSTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART C: DISTRIBUTION DIAGNOSTICS\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

cat("PURPOSE: Verify imputed values have plausible distributions.\n")
cat("  Red = observed, Blue = imputed. Distributions should be similar\n")
cat("  under MAR; systematic differences are not necessarily wrong but\n")
cat("  warrant scrutiny (van Buuren, 2018 §6.6).\n\n")

continuous_to_plot <- vars_to_plot[
  vars_to_plot %in% imp_params$variable_types$continuous]

if(length(continuous_to_plot) > 0) {
  vars_for_density <- head(continuous_to_plot, 8)
  cat("  Density plots for:", paste(vars_for_density, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  tryCatch({
    pdf("imputation_density_plots.pdf", width = 14, height = 10)
    print(densityplot(imp_final,
                      as.formula(paste("~", paste(vars_for_density, collapse = " + ")))))
    dev.off()
    cat("  ✓ Saved: imputation_density_plots.pdf\n\n")
  }, error = function(e)
    cat("  ⚠️  Density plot failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n\n"))
} else {
  cat("  No continuous variables available from plot list\n\n")
}

# Strip plots for categorical variables
ordered_to_plot <- vars_to_plot[vars_to_plot %in% imp_params$variable_types$ordered]
if(length(ordered_to_plot) > 0) {
  vars_for_strip <- head(ordered_to_plot, 6)
  tryCatch({
    pdf("imputation_stripplots.pdf", width = 12, height = 8)
    print(stripplot(imp_final,
                    as.formula(paste("~", paste(vars_for_strip, collapse = " + "))),
                    pch = 20, cex = 0.6))
    dev.off()
    cat("  ✓ Saved: imputation_stripplots.pdf\n\n")
  }, error = function(e)
    cat("  ⚠️  Stripplot failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n\n"))
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART D: STATISTICAL VERIFICATION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# These checks confirm the imputation is statistically sound before analysis.
# Each check targets a specific failure mode.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART D: STATISTICAL VERIFICATION\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

# Convenience: list of all imputed datasets
all_imp_list <- lapply(seq_len(imp_params$optimal_m),
                       function(i) mice::complete(imp_final, i))

# ── D1. Completeness check ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("D1. Completeness check\n")
cat("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  PURPOSE: Confirm every imputed variable has zero missing values\n")
cat("           in every completed dataset. Any remaining NAs indicate\n")
cat("           a variable that was supposed to be imputed but was not.\n\n")

imp_vars <- names(imp_params$method[imp_params$method != ""])
completeness_fails <- character()

for(i in seq_along(all_imp_list)) {
  d <- all_imp_list[[i]]
  for(var in imp_vars) {
    if(var %in% names(d) && anyNA(d[[var]]))
      completeness_fails <- c(completeness_fails,
                              sprintf("  Imputation %d, variable: %s", i, var))
  }
}

if(length(completeness_fails) == 0) {
  cat("  ✓ PASS — All", length(imp_vars), "imputed variables are complete",
      "across all", imp_params$optimal_m, "datasets\n\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("  ✗ FAIL — %d incompleteness issues detected:\n",
              length(completeness_fails)))
  for(msg in head(completeness_fails, 20)) cat("   ", msg, "\n")
  cat("\n")
}

# ── D2. Range preservation check (PMM) ───────────────────────────────────────
```
